The spectrum of $X$ is $\{\pm(p-1)\}$ (each once) together with $\pm 1$ (each with multiplicity $p-1$), using Ramanujan sums $c_{2p}(k)$. Vertices $0$ and $p$ are the antipodal pair, and the amplitude from $0$ to $x$ is $\frac{1}{2p}\sum_k e^{-i\lambda_k t}e^{2\pi i kx/2p}$. Requiring zero amplitude at every $x\notin\{0,p\}$ forces $\sin((p-1)t)=-\sin t$ and $\cos((p-1)t)=\cos t$, which together give $pt\equiv 0 \pmod{2\pi}$. So the support of $U(t)|0\rangle$ lies in $\{0,p\}$ exactly at $t=2\pi m/p$, and at $t=2\pi/p$ the state is $\cos(2\pi/p)\,|0\rangle + i\sin(2\pi/p)\,|p\rangle$. The minimum positive time is therefore $t^*=2\pi/p$. (Check at $p=3$: $X=C_6$, and the amplitudes computed from the spectrum are consistent.)

- Solution 1 uses $\lambda_{\max}=p-1$ and claims the revival time is $2\pi/(p-1)$. The spectrum has $\pm(p-1)$, but the revival condition depends on the full spectrum, not just the top eigenvalue, so this is wrong.
- Solution 2 gives $\pi$ with no derivation, relying on an unsupported "standard result." It is wrong.
- Solution 3 gives $p$ by conflating the antipodal distance with the revival time, and its eigenvalue analysis is abandoned mid-way. It is wrong.
